start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,559 words at about 125 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 5, Movement 2 to 6, Movement 4 to 7, Application to 6. Keep the pool, “One thing I know,” and the finding. Never cut the man never asking, the mud and the pool, the casting out and finding, or the worship in the street.
start_here_guardrails: Do not turn John 9:3 into a formula: not every suffering is “for God’s glory.” Jesus says it about this man, in this story.
Keep the archaeology in its place: the pool is real; the miracle remains a claim the text asks you to trust.
Track the man’s growing Christology. He is a witness still learning, not an instant theologian.
Do not cartoon the Pharisees. The group was divided, and the parents’ fear was real. The warning is for the church too.
Protect the casting out, the finding, the worship, the invitation, and the silence.
start_here_evidence: The Pool of Siloam, the mud, the man’s four confessions, and the parents’ fear are doing theological work.

slides.run: A SERMON FOR THE PULPIT · 55–60 MINUTES

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
lines: The light comes to the man
slides.note: The light of the world walked toward a man who had no idea he was waiting for it.

slides.label: 02 · THE STREET
slides.headline: A case file with a heartbeat.
panel: The disciples saw a theological problem.

slides.label: 03 · THE MAKING
slides.headline: He went. He washed. He came back seeing.

columns.note: He walks in the dark by trust.
The light is not a theory.

panel: That is what faith looks like in the dark.

slides.label: 04 · THE POOL
slides.headline: The pool that is still there.
slides.body: He could not see the water or the path. He went because the man who made mud told him to. The pool is real — the tunnel, the inscription, the 2004 discovery. The miracle is still a claim you must trust.
slides.pullquote: He walked to the pool in the dark. He came back in the light.
slides.footline: The evidence is real. It is not the same thing as faith.

slides.label: 05 · THE INTERROGATION
slides.headline: The room wants a better answer.
slides.quote: “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
slides.aside1: They have a doctrine of the man. They do not have his eyes.
slides.aside2: The parents go quiet. The neighbors disagree. The man keeps telling the truth.
slides.footline: “Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I know: I was blind, now I see.” — John 9:25

slides.label: 06 · THE VERDICT
slides.footline: Same man. Two verdicts. One of them is true.

slides.label: 07 · THE FINDING
slides.banner_main: “Do you believe in the Son of Man?”
lines: The first face he saw was the face of the one who healed him.
“Lord, I believe.” Worship in the street.
slides.footline: Thrown out of the house of God, he worships the Son of God in the street.

slides.label: 08 · THE GOSPEL
slides.banner_main: “I came into this world for judgment.”
lines: He did not come for the people who got it right.
He came for the people who found out they were blind.
slides.footline: The warning at the end of the chapter is for the church too.

slides.label: 09 · THE RESPONSE
slides.headline: What do you do with the light?

title: Stop writing
the case file.
items.desc: “Whose fault is it?” is not the first question. Look at the person in front of you.

title: Say what
you know.
items.desc: You do not need every answer. Tell the truth about your own eyes.

title: Go looking for
the cast-out.
items.desc: Someone near you was shown the door. Jesus is already outside.

title: Worship before
you see it all.
items.desc: The man believed with a partial Christology and a whole heart.

slides.footline: The light is not a theory. It is a person.

slides.label: 10 · THE INVITATION
slides.line1: Not try harder. Not see better. Come to the light.
lines: You can tell him what you do not know.
You can say what you do know. You can come.

slides.line2: And the man who never asked became a witness.
slides.body: The light is still walking toward people who have not asked.
